description: A qualitative analysis application you use in conversation with Claude, compatible with QualCoder: create projects, read, search and code your qualitative data, edit the codebook, write memos and export, in project files on this computer.
long_description:
Exegete (formerly qualcoder-mcp) is a qualitative analysis application you use in conversation with Claude, compatible with QualCoder. With Claude, you start projects, bring in documents and transcripts, read them with their codings, search, code them with suggestions you approve, edit the codebook, write memos, and export your codebook, coding and counts. Your projects are folders on this computer in QualCoder's format, so you can work on them in either program, one at a time. QualCoder is free software for qualitative analysis; Exegete is an independent project, not part of QualCoder and not made by its developers.

Exegete takes a backup of the project before every change to its database. Exegete runs on this computer and adds no telemetry of its own (on Windows x64, a library it installs for PDFs reports its use: PRIVACY.md), but what its tools return enters the conversation and is sent to Anthropic like any other chat content: read PRIVACY.md before you use research data (https://github.com/nicotem/exegete/blob/main/PRIVACY.md). Once a week at most, and when you ask, it fetches a small file from its website, which GitHub hosts, to see whether a newer version exists; nothing from your projects is sent, and the setting "Tell me when a new version is out" switches it off.

The settings choose the tool set (every tool, or a smaller set for local models), the folder where new projects and working copies are kept, your coder name and the AI coder name, whether you also use QualCoder on this computer, and whether Exegete tells you when a new version is out.

small_toolset.title: Limit Exegete to its small tool set
small_toolset.description: On: Exegete offers its small tool set, for a local model with little room for the tools' descriptions; that set cannot create a project. Off, the default: Exegete offers every tool. Settings take effect after Claude Desktop is quit and opened again.

projects_folder.title: Folder for projects
projects_folder.description: Where Exegete creates new projects and keeps working copies of projects. The default, Exegete projects in your home folder, is made when the first project needs it. Choose a folder that no sync service keeps. Leaving it empty stops the extension from starting.

coder_name.title: Your coder name
coder_name.description: The name your own codings carry in a project, kept apart from the AI's; Exegete gives it to each project it creates. Empty, the default: Claude asks for it at each new project. It must differ from the AI coder name.

ai_coder_name.title: AI coder name
ai_coder_name.description: The name Claude's work in a project is stored under, kept apart from yours and given to each project Exegete creates; a model's name lets different models' work be compared. Empty, the default: Claude asks the first time a project needs it.

i_use_qualcoder.title: I use QualCoder on this computer
i_use_qualcoder.description: On: Exegete adds some notes that matter only if you also open your projects in QualCoder. Off, the default: only when it finds signs of QualCoder on the project or this computer. Either way, it still checks whether QualCoder has a project open.

update_check.title: Tell me when a new version is out
update_check.description: On, the default: once a week at most, and when you ask, Exegete fetches a file naming the newest version from its website, which GitHub hosts. Nothing from your projects is sent; GitHub records your computer's internet address. Off: Exegete itself makes no connection.
